Subject: MAP: Data handling & compliance - milestone review

Thanks again for the time today — great to hear more about Acme's deployment goals and PHI constraints. Per our call, I'm attaching the draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with the Data handling & compliance milestone sketched out. Key items in this milestone: retention, logging & audit trails, PHI/PII constraints, and required evidence (SOC 2 + DPA).

Proposed milestone (Data handling & compliance):
- Target close date: 2026-08-20
- Responsibility: Acme (security review & procurement), Redwood (evidence + config)
- Deliverables: DPA & contract redline, SOC 2 artifact package, config checklist (retention, encryption, audit logging), deployment diagram for private VPC
- Dependencies: Procurement timeline, SOC 2 artifact access, access to test environment for validation

Action items I propose next: please confirm the responsibilities above, confirm target close date or propose an alternative, and I'll get Neha to draft the technical checklist and Rishi to prepare the SOC 2 package. I've attached the MAP draft and a one-page data-handling redlines doc.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance - milestone review

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. The milestone looks good overall. A few clarifications from our side:
1) PHI: We need explicit confirmation that Redwood supports isolation of PHI at rest and in transit, and that logs containing PHI/PII can be redacted or excluded from long-term retention.
2) Retention: Our policy is 7 years for clinical records; for logs we typically retain 2 years, but we need the option to configure retention per env.
3) Evidence: SOC 2 is required; a DPA and details on encryption (KMS/HSM) also required.

Timeline: procurement has a monthly cadence; if we can finalize redlines by 2026-08-10, that keeps us on track for an internal approval window.

I'll review the attached MAP and redlines doc and circle back with any edits. Looping in Priya for security sign-off.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior IT Project Manager | Acme Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance - milestone review (internal)

Quick internal note on the technical checklist that Acme requested:
- PHI handling: Redwood supports VPC-private deployments and customer-managed keys (KMS). For PHI we recommend Private deployment + customer-managed KMS; we can also offer token-level redaction for logs so PII/PHI fields are masked before any long-term storage.
- Retention config: retention is configurable by route/env. Default logs retention is 90 days; can extend to 2 years via our retention policy configs (requires Dedicated or Private).
- Audit trails: we can provide per-request audit logs with request/response metadata; full request bodies containing PHI can be excluded or stored in a short-lived store for validation only.
- Evidence: Rishi, can you confirm what SOC 2 artifacts we can share (control library, last audit report, and scope)? Also will prepare an evidence pack we can upload to the shared Drive.

I recommend we propose the technical checklist to Acme with two config options: (A) Hosted with token redaction + strict retention (if they accept hosted), or (B) Private deployment with customer KMS and extended retention. Will draft language and share a short matrix.

-Neha

- Dependencies: procurement redline turnaround, access to test environment for validation (we'll need a short-lived staging dataset), final PHI scoping from Acme (fields + flows)

Next steps / asks for Acme:

2) Confirm whether you prefer Option A (Hosted + token redaction) or Option B (Private + customer KMS) so we can prioritize the runbook.
3) Provide contact for procurement who will receive the DocuSign link for contract redlines.

I've uploaded the updated MAP and the one-page redlines doc to the shared Drive (link below) and initiated a DocuSign envelope for the DPA so procurement can sign.
